original_question: If a Banach space X is strongly weakly compactly generated, must the Lebesgue-Bochner space L^1(μ, X) also be strongly weakly compactly generated?
target_in_paper: Problem 5.2 (Schlüchtermann-Wheeler, [113]): Is the space L^1(μ, X) SWCG whenever X is?
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the correct open problem in the paper: the permanence question asking whether the strongly weakly compactly generated (SWCG) property of a Banach space X passes to the Lebesgue-Bochner space L^1(μ, X). It also uses the correct exponent p = 1 and the correct target property SWCG, rather than the neighboring questions about WCG, WKA, WCD, or weak* sequential compactness.
missing_details: The paper's Section 5 fixes an arbitrary probability space (Ω, Σ, μ); the problem is intended with this ambient hypothesis, so the quantification over μ should be explicit rather than left implicit.
The paper works throughout with real Banach spaces, so the scalar field should be stated if the question is to be fully paper-faithful and stand-alone.
SWCG should be defined explicitly: there exists a weakly compact set K0 ⊂ X such that for every weakly compact K ⊂ X and every ε > 0, one has K ⊂ nK0 + ε B_X for some n ∈ N.
L^1(μ, X) should be identified as the Lebesgue-Bochner space of equivalence classes of strongly measurable X-valued functions f with ∫Ω ||f(ω)|| dμ(ω) < ∞.
The universal quantifier should be made explicit: the question is whether for every probability space and every SWCG Banach space X, the corresponding space L^1(μ, X) is SWCG.
refined_question: For every probability space (Ω, Σ, μ) and every real Banach space X, suppose X is strongly weakly compactly generated, meaning that there exists a weakly compact set K0 ⊂ X such that for every weakly compact set K ⊂ X and every ε > 0 there is n ∈ N with K ⊂ nK0 + ε B_X, where B_X is the closed unit ball of X. Must the Lebesgue-Bochner space L^1(μ, X), consisting of equivalence classes of strongly measurable functions f: Ω → X such that ∫Ω ||f(ω)|| dμ(ω) < ∞, also be strongly weakly compactly generated?
justification: This is exactly the paper's Problem 5.2 in §5.1, not a broader neighboring question. Your draft already preserves the right implication, the right exponent p = 1, and the right property SWCG. To make it fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one must import the section-wide setup that (Ω, Σ, μ) is a probability space and that L^p(μ, X) denotes the usual Lebesgue-Bochner space of strongly measurable functions (§5, p. 13), together with the paper's standing convention that Banach spaces are real (Notation and terminology, p. 2) and the earlier definition of SWCG (§1.3, p. 5). The nearby discussion in §5.1 also confirms that this is the intended open permanence problem and records the known positive cases (p. 14).
